rounds.text: Anuh Pharma is significantly undervalued relative to its peers, trading at a P/E of 17.72x [E6] and an EV/EBITDA of 11.34x [E11] against sector benchmarks of 30.8x [E6] and 16.42x [E11]. Despite this discount, the company outperforms the sector in core efficiency metrics, delivering an ROCE of 17.28% [E10] and an ROA of 8.63% [E8] compared to sector medians of 11.76% [E10] and 6.4% [E8]. Recent performance highlights a sharp acceleration, with trailing twelve-month profit growth of 23% [E21] and a year-over-year net profit surge of 38% [E62]. This growth is supported by a robust balance sheet that is almost debt-free [E58] with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.05x [E37], while promoters have demonstrated confidence by increasing their stake to 71.79% [E40]. Current market pricing implies only 6.0% earnings growth [E46], which sits well below the 10.0% base case [E46] and leaves a 25.5% margin of safety [E45] relative to its intrinsic value of Rs 109 [E44]. Conceded: [E30] and [E35], the company reported negative operating cash flow of Rs -3 Cr in March 2026 [E35] and a trailing twelve-month operating margin that has contracted by 3 percentage points over the last three years [E30]. However, with expanding quarterly margins [E31, E64], a relative-strength rating of 76 [E50], and a rules-based buy score of 77 out of 100 [E61], the business appears fundamentally under-appreciated [E6, E11, E44, E45].

Anuh Pharma Ltd carries significant underlying operational risks that contradict its headline valuation multiples and optical growth figures [E18, E34, E36]. The most alarming vulnerability is the collapse in cash generation, evidenced by operating cash flow dropping to negative ₹3 Cr and free cash flow plunging to negative ₹11 Cr for Mar 2026, leading to a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -0.07x [E34, E35, E36]. This severe disconnect between reported earnings and actual cash realization is compounded by a sudden leveraging of the balance sheet, with borrowings rising from ₹0 Cr to ₹19 Cr within a single year as of Sep 2026 [E38]. Long-term wealth creation for shareholders has also stagnated, demonstrated by a paltry 4% compounded profit growth and a meager 4% compounded share price growth over 10 years, alongside a negative 9% share price return over the past year [E18, E22, E25]. Profitability metrics further expose structural mediocrity, highlighted by a low 3-year average return on equity of 13.8% and a multi-year erosion in operating margins from 12% down to 9% in the TTM period [E30, E60]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.05x, demonstrates recent positive momentum in quarterly margins, and trades at a discount to sector valuation benchmarks [E6, E7, E11, E31, E37].

Conceded: borrowings increased to ₹19 Cr in Sep 2026 from ₹0 Cr a year earlier, and 10-year compounded profit and share price growth stand at a modest 4% [E18, E22, E38]. However, the company remains almost debt free with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.05x as of Sep 2026 [E37, E58]. Furthermore, trailing twelve-month profit growth has accelerated sharply to 23%, and quarterly operating margins expanded by 3 percentage points to 9% in Sep 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E21, E31]. Long-term returns continue to outpace sector benchmarks, with an ROA of 8.63% against 6.4%, an ROE of 13.27% against 10.57%, and an ROCE of 17.28% against 11.76% [E8, E9, E10]. Finally, promoter confidence is rising as holdings increased by 1.85 percentage points to 71.79% in Sep 2026, accompanied by positive institutional money flow [E40, E43].

Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.05x [E37]. However, borrowings have newly surged from zero to ₹19 Cr [E38], directly undermining the notion of a debt-free status. While trailing profit growth reached 23% [E21], this short-term metric masks a stagnant 10-year compounded profit growth of just 4% [E18] and a 3-year profit growth of only 3% [E20], alongside an actual sales decline of -1% YoY noted in the screens [E66]. Although quarterly operating margins expanded by 3 percentage points [E31], the broader structural trend reveals a multi-year margin compression, with TTM operating margins dropping to 9% from 12% three years prior [E30], driven by inconsistent operational execution [E32, E33]. Conceded: sector-beating ROE and ROCE figures are present [E8, E9, E10]; nevertheless, the company’s own historical returns remain low, capped by a 3-year average ROE of only 13.8% [E60]. Finally, while promoter holdings increased [E40], this inside accumulation has failed to translate into shareholder wealth, as the 1-year share price return sits at -9% [E25] and the Sharpe ratio remains deeply negative at -0.12 [E54].
